clue.text: Comic character from TV series in busy pub-theatre run

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run

indicators.note: the TV series sits in the middle of the jumbled letters
a busy scene is all bustle and movement, so the letters of pub-theatre and R are jumbled

parts.note: ER is the long-running American hospital drama

explanation.surface: A cartoon figure from television turns up in a pub theatre's crowded season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'busy' shuffles PUBTHEATRE; 'in' sets the TV series inside that. Rupert the Bear is the checked-trousered bear of a long-running British newspaper comic strip and annual.
explanation.definitionFit: Rupert is a cartoon bear from a newspaper strip, so he is a character in a comic.

clue.text: Ideal university will prepare one for student

indicators.note: for means instead of, so one takes the student's place

parts.note: read as an intention, 'will prepare' is TO PLAN
L is the learner, a student
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A perfect university readies each newcomer for student life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one for student' swaps the L (learner, the student) in TO PLAN for I, giving TOPIAN after U.
explanation.definitionFit: A utopian scheme is perfect but unreal, so the adjective means ideal.

clue.text: Base vote on case for independent withdrawal

parts.note: e is the base of natural logarithms in maths
a cross, X, marks a vote on a ballot paper

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outside letters, here those of independent

explanation.surface: A political base votes on the argument for withdrawing from a union to stand alone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case for' takes the first and last letters of 'independent', IT.
explanation.definitionFit: An exit is a departure, the act of leaving or pulling out.

clue.text: Teach your extremely old papers — you've got some neck?

indicators.note: the extremes of each word are its first and last letters

parts.note: ID means identity papers

explanation.surface: A cheeky jibe at someone presuming to teach an elder something from yellowed papers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'You've got some neck' sounds like an accusation of cheek; read literally, it says you have a gland in your neck.
explanation.definitionFit: The thyroid gland sits in the front of the throat, so everyone has one in the neck.

clue.text: It's in joints like the man's hands gripping

indicators.note: the two hands grip, so they hold the other pieces between them

parts.note: H is an abbreviation for hand, twice here for two hands
as can mean like, as in 'dressed as a pirate'
the man's belongings are his

explanation.surface: A man's hands clutching something as if in a carpenter's joints.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gripping' needs two hands, one at each end, closing round the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Hashish is cannabis resin, often smoked rolled into joints, cannabis cigarettes.

clue.text: Blow fly

definitions.meaning: to ... along is to move at speed

explanation.surface: A short instruction to puff an insect away.
explanation.definitionFit: A belt is a heavy punch, and to belt is to race along at speed.

clue.text: Embarrasses adult son taking party drug

indicators.note: the adult and son take the party and drug in between them

parts.note: A is the film certificate for adult
a bash is a party
E is ecstasy

explanation.surface: A grown man shames his son by taking drugs at a party.
explanation.definitionFit: To abash someone is to make them ashamed or self-conscious.

clue.text: Heart essentially clear after plug controls unstable angina repeatedly

indicators.note: the heart and clear pieces come after the plug piece
the ad holds, so controls, the shuffled letters inside it

parts.note: a plug is an advertisement, AD

indicators.note: unstable letters are shaky, so the letters of angina move
the essence of a word is its central letter, from heart

parts.note: to clear a profit is to gain

explanation.surface: A medical picture: a stent controlling unstable angina after the heart is cleared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unstable' rearranges angina to AGAINAN inside the plug; 'essentially' takes the central letter of heart. The medical surface hides that 'plug' is an advert.
explanation.definitionFit: Again and again is an idiom for over and over, done many times.

clue.text: Beastly complaint diocese saw?

parts.note: MAD read as an anagram signal working on COW DISEASE gives the letters of diocese saw

explanation.surface: A bishop's territory witnessing an outbreak of something nasty.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer is the instruction. 'Mad' works as an anagram signal on COW DISEASE, whose letters rearrange to DIOCESE SAW.
explanation.definitionFit: Mad cow disease (BSE) is an illness of cattle, so a complaint afflicting beasts.

clue.text: Please make grass look right — leading to praise

indicators.note: 'make X Y' tells us to turn the informer into the new letters

parts.note: to gratify is to please
a grass is an informer, a rat
lo is an old word for look

explanation.surface: A gardener's instruction to make the lawn look right, leading to compliments.
explanation.walkthrough: In GRATIFY the RAT (grass, an informer) becomes LOR. 'Grass' here is the British slang for a police informer.
explanation.definitionFit: To glorify is to praise lavishly, a near synonym.

clue.text: Fantastic Santa Claus regularly gives fruit

indicators.note: fantastic suggests the letters are made fanciful and rearranged
taking letters at regular intervals from Claus gives its second and fourth

explanation.surface: Father Christmas reliably hands out dried fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes LU from Claus; with SANTA these letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A sultana is a dried seedless grape, a fruit used in cakes.

clue.text: Some boots I biked over for winger

indicators.note: over signals the letters are turned back to front
only some of the letters of these words are used

explanation.surface: A footballer's boots worn while out on a bike, for a wide player.
explanation.walkthrough: SIBI sits in 'bootS I BIked'; 'over' reads it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An ibis is a wading bird, and crosswords often call any bird a winger.

clue.text: Jerk outside leg, increasing strength

indicators.note: the twitch goes outside, around the leg side

parts.note: a tic is a jerky twitch
on is the leg side in cricket

explanation.surface: A twitch around the leg as a muscle builds power.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the leg side is also called the on side, so leg gives ON.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonic is invigorating, so as an adjective it means building up vigour.

clue.text: In ancient Rome, this goes on Caesar's head to be stylish

indicators.note: the Latin word goes on, follows, the first letter of the name
the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: hic is Latin for this

explanation.surface: Something placed on a Roman emperor's head, a laurel wreath perhaps, to look smart.
explanation.walkthrough: C (Caesar's head) comes first, then HIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Chic means elegantly fashionable.

clue.text: Dorothy Perkins's marketing executive?

indicators.note: the possessive says the word belongs to, is held in, the name

explanation.surface: Asks who handles the advertising for Dorothy Perkins, a British high-street women's clothing chain.
explanation.walkthrough: HYPER is held in 'dorotHY PERkins', the possessive marking what the name holds; one who hypes products is a hyper.
explanation.definitionFit: Marketing works by hype, so a marketer could whimsically be called a hyper.

clue.text: Where you stand to face the board after pocketing Republican money

indicators.note: the oche pockets, takes in, the Republican

parts.words: Where you stand to face the board
parts.note: the oche is the line darts players stand behind

explanation.surface: A darts player at the line, after gaining some cash.
explanation.walkthrough: The oche is the throwing line in British pub darts. Ochre is old slang for money, from gold coins.
explanation.definitionFit: Ochre is a slang term for money, from the colour of gold coins.

clue.text: Ant not yet rejecting terms — Dec's beginning to get upset

indicators.note: the terms are the end letters of each word, and they are dropped
the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Ant of the British TV presenting duo Ant and Dec declines terms, so Dec gets cross.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the final letter (a T each time) of Ant, not and yet to leave ANNOYE, then add D.
explanation.definitionFit: Annoyed and upset both describe being irritated or put out.

clue.text: Tool to gain unauthorised access was returned

parts.note: to hack is to break into a computer system

indicators.note: returned means the word was is turned back

explanation.surface: A burglar's implement, given back after a break-in.
explanation.definitionFit: A hacksaw is a fine-toothed saw for metal, a workshop tool.

clue.text: Group of narcs stop most expensive …

parts.note: the DEA is the US Drug Enforcement Administration, whose agents are narcs
to rest is to stop

explanation.surface: A US drug squad halting the priciest goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Dearest is the superlative of dear, meaning costly.

clue.text: Dawn Basra raid viable, every now and then

indicators.note: taking a letter every now and then picks alternate letters

explanation.surface: A military report that a dawn raid on Basra is workable only occasionally.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters of 'Basra raid viable' spell the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Dawn is the arrival of day, its first coming.

clue.text: Decorative pattern in salver describing church minister's end

indicators.note: describing in the sense of drawing around, so the tray encircles

parts.note: a salver is a serving tray
CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: An ornate engraving on a church minister's silver plate.
explanation.definitionFit: Tracery is ornamental interlacing stonework or design, a decorative pattern.

clue.text: … sort of car without, say, drawing rifle

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the car wraps the drawing

parts.note: the Mini is a classic British small car
drawing is an example of art

explanation.surface: Continues the previous clue: a car without a sketch of a gun.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis tempts a link to the cocktail; here the Martini-Henry was a Victorian British army rifle.
explanation.definitionFit: The Martini-Henry was a British breech-loading service rifle, often shortened to Martini.

clue.text: Great writing about opening for Abbott and Costello — perhaps recalled forgetting line

indicators.note: the manuscript goes about, around, the opening letter

parts.note: MS is a manuscript, a piece of writing

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter
forgetting means a letter is left out
recalled, called back, means the name is read backwards

parts.note: Elvis Costello is a singer, so Costello hints at the first name Elvis

explanation.surface: A tribute to the comedy duo Abbott and Costello, remembered without their lines.
explanation.walkthrough: Costello is not Lou of the comedy duo but the singer Elvis Costello; 'recalled' turns the name round to SIVLE before 'forgetting line' drops the L.
explanation.definitionFit: Massive and great both mean very large.

clue.text: Churchill's one to strengthen, holding small cigar butt

indicators.note: inure holds the small letter inside it

parts.note: to inure is to harden or toughen

indicators.note: a cigar butt is its end, the last letter

explanation.surface: Winston Churchill steeling himself, gripping a stubby cigar.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is Winston Churchill, but Churchill is also a British insurance company with a nodding-dog mascot.
explanation.definitionFit: Churchill is a UK insurance company, so it is one example of the business.

clue.text: Dress to boast about

indicators.note: about here means turned around, read backwards

parts.note: to brag is to boast

explanation.surface: An outfit worth showing off.
explanation.definitionFit: Garb is clothing or attire, a synonym for dress.

clue.text: Plant unknown on stage

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after

parts.note: a dais is a raised platform
y is an unknown in algebra

explanation.surface: A plant whose identity is a mystery, seen in a theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: A daisy is a common flowering plant.

clue.text: Man could be somewhat travel-sick, facing the wrong way

indicators.note: facing the wrong way means the letters read backwards
somewhat means only a part of the word is used

explanation.surface: A man looking a bit queasy, turned the wrong way on a journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is the Isle of Man, the island between Britain and Ireland; ELSI from 'travEL-SIck' is read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man is an island, so Man is an example of an isle.

clue.text: Discovered writer's home

indicators.note: dis-covered, with its covers removed, so the outer letters go

parts.note: a scribe is a writer

explanation.surface: An author's house is found.
explanation.walkthrough: SCRIBE loses its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Crib is slang for a person's home or house.

clue.text: Understand speaker's vote against

indicators.note: what a speaker says is heard rather than written

parts.note: a no is a vote against

explanation.surface: Grasp that the Speaker votes no.
explanation.definitionFit: To know something is to understand it.

clue.text: Flipside's hot against tongue

parts.note: hot means fashionable, in
V is versus, against
Erse is the Gaelic language

explanation.surface: The other side of a spicy rival language.
explanation.definitionFit: The inverse is the opposite, the reverse side of something.

clue.text: Works a way into hotels

indicators.note: the a and the way go into the hotels

parts.note: inns are small hotels
RD is road, a way

explanation.surface: Working out a route into several hotels.
explanation.definitionFit: The works of a machine are its internal mechanism, its inner parts.

clue.text: Blond Tory woke up those with friends in high places?

definitions.text: those with friends in high places?

indicators.note: up here means stirred up, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A fair-haired Conservative waking up among the well-connected elite.
explanation.walkthrough: The old boy network is the British public-school mutual-help circle.
explanation.definitionFit: The old boy network is the informal web of influential connections among former schoolmates.
